draft.title: Pork and Green Mango Soup

ingredients.note: Divided: some seared with spices, rest sliced into thin strips
Unripe sour green mangoes, cut into 1-inch strips

steps.text: Prepare and cook the rice according to package directions so it is ready for serving.
Chop bone-in pork ribs into small, bite-sized pieces.

why.text: Bone-in pork adds richer flavor to the broth.
why.quote: you want the porks with the bone on them 'cause the bone gives a little bit more flavor to the broth

steps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a quick boil and add the pork pieces. Boil briefly, then drain completely and discard the water.

why.text: Removes blood, scum, and gunk to keep broth clear and clean-tasting.
why.quote: get rid of all the blood and the scum and all the gunk that comes off of the bone that adds a weird flavor to this soup and makes it a little cloudy I don't like those extra proteins and collagens and all that stuff floating around I like crystal clear broth

steps.text: Fill the pot again with fresh water, bring to a boil with the pork, and skim off any remaining foam from the top. Strain and pat pork dry.

why.text: Drying the boiled meat ensures it sears properly in hot oil rather than steaming.

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot or pan over medium-high heat. Test the temperature by dipping a wooden chopstick into the oil until bubbles form around the tip.
Sear the pork pieces until golden brown on all sides.
Add cracked black pepper, then add fish sauce. Cook for about 30 seconds until the fish sauce reduces slightly and the pepper releases its aroma.

why.text: Allows pepper to bloom in heat and fish sauce to concentrate flavor.
why.quote: give it about like a 32nd so that the fish house tries and the cracked black pepper uh reese's it's aroma

steps.text: Add part of the chopped onion and sear until slightly translucent, scraping up any brown bits stuck to the bottom of the pan.
Pour in fresh water and return the pork to the pot if seared in a separate pan. Simmer for 30 to 60 minutes until the pork is tender.
Slice the remaining white onions into thin strips, chop the green onions into small pieces, chop the cilantro, and slice the unripe green mangoes into 1-inch strips.

why.text: White onions are less sweet, which balances the sweet and sour fruit profile.
why.quote: I don't like onions to be a little too sweet in this soup 'cause there's a fruit component and the fruits are a sweet and sour

steps.text: Once the pork is tender, add the green mango strips to the pot. Cook for 5 to 10 minutes until slightly softened.

why.text: Softens crunchy raw mango and releases its sourness into the broth.
why.quote: you just want to cook it down so that I release it sourness and blends all the flavor together

steps.text: Stir in the sliced white onions, green onions, and fresh cilantro right at the end of cooking.
Ladle the hot soup over cooked rice in bowls. Top with sliced chili peppers for heat if desired.

notes: Step order reordered: rice prep listed first so it can cook while soup is prepared.
Dictation fix: 'test up the chopstick make sure that the chopsticks boiling' interpreted as testing oil heat with a wooden chopstick.
Dictation fix: 'fish house tries' corrected to 'fish sauce dries/reduces'.
Dictation fix: 'reese's it's aroma' corrected to 'releases its aroma'.
Self-correction noted: cook corrected spice order to pepper first, then fish sauce.
Green onions were cut in transcript but not explicitly added step included green onions with final aromatic herbs.

questions.quote: cut up pork ribs into tiny little chunks
questions.question: How many pounds of pork ribs should be used for this soup?
questions.why_it_matters: Without a weight, the meat-to-broth ratio will be unbalanced.
questions.suggestion: 2 pounds bone-in pork spare ribs or baby back ribs.

questions.question: How many cups or quarts of water should be added for the broth?
questions.why_it_matters: Too much water makes a bland soup, while too little leaves insufficient broth.

questions.quote: you add oil to the pot or you add oil to a different pan
questions.question: Do you prefer searing the pork in the same pot used for soup, or in a separate skillet?
questions.why_it_matters: Using a single pot preserves all seared flavors and reduces cleanup.
questions.suggestion: Sear directly in the heavy soup pot.

questions.quote: throw in the onions... slice up white onions
questions.question: Are onions added twice (once chopped while searing meat, and once sliced at the end)?
questions.why_it_matters: First-time cooks won't know how to divide the onions between searing and finishing.
questions.suggestion: Use 1 medium white onion: half finely chopped for searing, half sliced into thin strips for finishing.

questions.quote: cook the mangoes for about 5 minutes... after 10 minutes
questions.question: How long should the green mangoes simmer in the broth?
questions.why_it_matters: Overcooked mangoes turn mushy and disintegrate into the broth.
questions.suggestion: Simmer for 5 to 7 minutes until tender-firm.

questions.quote: put your fish sauce in... first you add your pepper
questions.question: How much fish sauce and black pepper should be added?
questions.why_it_matters: Fish sauce provides the primary saltiness and umami for the soup base.
questions.suggestion: 2 tablespoons fish sauce and 1/2 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper.

questions.quote: green mangoes you want the mangoes to be really sour
questions.question: Is there a specific brand or variety of green mango (or substitute like green papaya) you prefer?
questions.why_it_matters: Ripe yellow mangoes will make the soup overly sweet instead of sour.
questions.suggestion: Unripe firm green Kent or Tommy Atkins mangoes from an Asian market.

draft.title: Tomato Tofu

ingredients.note: Type not specified (e.g., firm or extra firm). Cook notes some pieces left lighter/creamier and some fried crispy.
Diced. Cook added extra during cooking as they reduced.
Cut into little strips. Dictated as 'in onions'.

Cook indicated amount with a visual gesture.
Used for sautéing and deep-frying tofu.
Added to loosen tomato sauce while simmering.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Dice 5 tomatoes into small pieces, slice onions into thin strips, and chop 5 garlic cloves.
Deep-fry the tofu: Heat oil in a pan until a wooden chopstick inserted into the oil forms small bubbles. Add the tofu pieces. Fry until light yellow, or continue until golden and crispy.

why.text: Keep some pieces lightly cooked so they stay creamy, and fry others golden and crispy so they absorb sauce better.
why.quote: sister likes the tofu less cooked so it's creamier so we'll keep a couple pieces less cooked and then we'll keep a couple pieces that are cooked very golden and crispy so it can absorb the sauce

dials.effect: Chewier texture that absorbs sauce well

steps.text: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat until a chopstick sizzles when inserted.
Add the fish sauce to the hot oil before it gets too hot. Let it start bubbling.

why.text: Add fish sauce early before the pan gets way too hot.
why.quote: add a little bit of fish sauce before it gets way too hot and burns everything

steps.text: Once the fish sauce liquid stops bubbling and starts sticking to the bottom of the pan, immediately add the sliced onions with their juices and stir constantly.

why.text: The onion juices cool down the pan so the fish sauce does not burn.
why.quote: you want to get all the juices to cool down the pan so it doesn't burn the fish sauce

steps.text: Stir in the 5 cloves of chopped garlic. Sauté for 7 minutes until soft and golden.

why.text: Cooking longer adds extra sweetness to the dish.
why.quote: yeah let's do it 7 minutes I want a little bit of sweeter today

steps.text: Add the diced tomatoes. Cook for about 2 minutes to allow them to slightly caramelize before adding any water.

why.text: Caramelizing the tomatoes gives the dish a meaty depth of flavor.
why.quote: you wanted 2 minutes to slightly caramelize too before you add the water because that can caramelize tomato adds a really meaty touch to the dish

steps.text: Add a splash of water if the tomatoes become too dry. Add the fried tofu and simmer together for 5 to 10 minutes until flavors combine.

why.text: Simmering allows the tofu to absorb the tomato and fish sauce flavors into its center.
why.quote: simmer it so the water extract all the flavor from the sauce tomato fish sauce into the inner parts of the tofu

steps.text: Serve hot over steamed white rice. Provide a small dipping dish with soy sauce and sliced chili on the side.

Self-correction: Cook increased sautéing time from 5 minutes to 7 minutes for a sweeter flavor.

draft.title: Homemade Sweetened Yogurt

steps.text: Heat 1/2 gallon of milk in a pot over medium heat until it steams slightly, making sure it does not reach a boil.

why.text: Prevent boiling while heating until steam appears.
why.quote: make sure it doesn't boil uh just until it steams a little bit

why.text: Heating milk denatures proteins, which creates a firmer yogurt structure.

steps.text: Stir 1/3 cup of sugar (or less, according to preference) into the warm milk until fully dissolved.
Mix the plain unflavored yogurt into the milk mixture until thoroughly blended.
Pour the milk mixture into individual small jars.
Place the jars into the incubator and let sit for 8 to 12 hours.
Transfer the jars to the refrigerator to chill, or freeze them before serving.

notes: Flagged missing cooling step before adding yogurt culture to protect live bacteria.
Identified possible dictation error in '10 in yogurt container'.

questions.question: Should the heated milk be allowed to cool down before stirring in the yogurt culture?
questions.why_it_matters: Adding live yogurt cultures to steaming hot milk kills the beneficial bacteria, preventing the yogurt from setting.
questions.suggestion: Cool the milk to 110°F (43°C) before adding the yogurt culture.

questions.question: What brand or size of plain yogurt container was meant by '10 in'?
questions.why_it_matters: Using the wrong proportion of starter yogurt affects fermentation speed and yogurt consistency.
questions.suggestion: Use 2 to 3 tablespoons (or a small 6 oz container) of plain, unflavored yogurt with live active cultures, such as Dannon.

questions.question: What temperature or setting should be used for the incubator?
questions.why_it_matters: Incorrect incubation temperatures can kill the culture or allow unwanted bacteria to grow.
questions.suggestion: Maintain a warm environment around 108°F–110°F (42°C–43°C) in a yogurt maker, food dehydrator, or warm oven.
